reviews.review: its a cool idea but the problem is that i dont have friends. there isnt any AI you can play against (except the 2 tutorials), and the public lobbies take ages to fill
reviews.developer_response:
Thank you for taking the time to leave a review and for trying the game in its early adopter phase.
You’re absolutely right: right now it’s very hard to find someone to play with, and it’s common to sit in the queue without getting a match.

From day one we’ve known that concurrency (getting enough people online at the same moment) would be the hardest part of launching a real-time online game that’s primarily focused on PvP with a small player base, and we’ve been building systems specifically to address this as part of our early adopter roadmap.

Our latest test version includes a Game Time Match system and supporting features that:

- Encourage players to jump in during specific game times tuned for different regions (Americas / Europe–Africa / Asia–Pacific), so people naturally overlap more.

- Clearly show in-game when it’s a good time to play, with a dedicated Game Time Match button and status text like “PLAYING NOW!” for your region.

We are also working on growing the player base through our Steam and Discord communities. Please consider joining our Discord and being part of the group that helps shape these early systems:
https://discord.gg/7bvx8qxR

We are also working on adding AI opponents to fill empty slots in a future update, so that low player counts don’t prevent you from getting a full match.

We genuinely believe this can be a very fun game once players are regularly meeting each other, since it’s built around fast, high-tension multiplayer chess variants (Square and Hex boards, FFA and team modes, different player counts). The design is meant to create lively, tactical, sometimes chaotic sessions rather than slow, grindy games.

Thanks again for the honest feedback and for checking out the game this early in its life.
